Name any retailer and chances are they're offering Black Friday TV deals today. For years, TVs have been the rockstar of Black Friday deals and that remains true for 2026. But not every TV deal you'll find today is worth your time.

I've been covering Black Friday TV deals for 19 years. I even purchased my first OLED TV two Black Friday ago. So when it comes to deal hunting, consider me your expert guide. I'll help you navigate through the maze of TV deals and spotlight the discounts on the TVs the Tom's Guide staff has tested, recommends, or has purchased.

My top pick today is the Hisense 75-inch U6 Pro Mini-LED 4K TV for $699 at Amazon. In our Hisense U6SF Pro review we called the Editor's Choice TV one of this year's best budget TVs. The 55-, 65-, and 75-inch models are all at their lowest price of the year starting from $469.

Make sure to bookmark this page as we bring you more of the best Black Friday TV deals today. For a wider look at this week's sales, check out our Black Friday deals guide.

The Ember Artline is Amazon's take on the art TV competing with the likes of Samsung's The Frame. It features a matte 4K QLED display that, like The Frame, can act as artwork when you're not watching shows or movies. Instead of Tizen, however, the Artline comes with the new Fire TV operating system that received an overhaul this past February, as well as access to Alexa+.

The TCL QM6K has been a Tom's Guide go-to recommendation for some time now, especially if you're on a budget and looking to spend less than $1,000. The 4K Mini-LED TV offers better brightness and backlight control than pricier competitors, supports 4K gaming at 120Hz, and if you hook up a gaming PC, the QM6K supports 4K at 144Hz. It's an all-around crowd pleaser.

In our Hisense U6SF Pro review, we called the U6 Pro one of the best budget Mini-LED TVs out there. All models are on sale, but the 75-inch model is such an epic bargain at this price point. Two of its four HDMI inputs feature 2.1 functionality (like support for 4K games up to 144Hz), and the screen is outfitted with a glare-free finish that actually works. If you're on a budget, enjoy mostly daytime viewing, and are an avid gamer, this TV is for you.

The QM7L is a fantastic way to experience TCL's SQD Mini-LED technology for much less than what you'll spend on a higher-end model. We recently awarded this TV a 4.5-star rating for its sensational color, its thorough collection of features, and its fantastically bright picture.

The C6 is LG's flagship OLED TV for 2026. In our LG C6 OLED TV review we said the Editor's Choice TV performs brilliantly offering top-tier brightness and colors. We're also fans of its gameplay enhancing features including a new Game Optimizer mode that obliterates input lag and boosts FPS on both consoles and PCs. Whether you're a gamer, sports fan, or movie buff — you won't be disappointed with the C6.

Good afternoon, shoppers! I'm Louis, deals editor-in-chief at Tom's Guide. I've been covering retail holidays for 19 years (!) and Thanksgiving Week is my favorite time of year to buy just about anything. But TVs in particular tend to see the biggest price drops this week.

While it's true that you can find good TV deals throughout the year (like on Presidents' Day, Labor Day, etc) the very best TV deals happen in November/December. And I'm not just saying that — I myself waited till November to buy my first OLED TV. (The now old, but still amazing LG C2 if you're wondering).

Simply put, the next few days will see the lowest prices on the TVs that are actually worth buying. If you have a shopping question or just want to let me know what deals you're looking for — or what TV you've already purchased — drop me a note! Now on to the deals....

Holy smokes, this is an amazing deal. The LG C6 is hands-down one of the best OLED TVs of 2026. It offers spectacular OLED performance (including ample brightness) and comes with a full slate of four HDMI 2.1 inputs, Dolby Vision support, and just about every gaming-related feature a dedicated gamer could ask for.

It's on sale at its second-lowest price ever and Best Buy is bundling a free $100 gift card. (By comparison, Amazon has the same price sans gift card). It did hit $1,349 earlier this month, but that freebie gift card makes up for the $50 difference in my opinion.

Buying an OLED TV has been one of the best tech purchases I've ever made. My OLED TV provides images that are sharp and realistic. This is especially true when watching dark, k-dramas like My Mister and Lost (both of which I recommend 100% btw).

If you're looking to buy your first OLED, this is the TV I'd buy.

Let me start by saying that we didn't give the 2026 Roku Select Series TV the best review. Yes, it's very affordable, but my colleague Sean Captain said its generally disappointing and you might be better off with the 2025 Roku Plus Series for $299 (if you can still find stock).

However, my mom has the Select Series TV in her living room and I quite like it. The Roku interface is super easy to navigate and the image quality — while not the best — is decent for the price.

If you want a TV with stunning picture quality that'll be the centerpiece of your living room — I'd say look elsewhere. But if you're not super critical and/or just want a budget TV for the bedroom — it's a solid pick now that it's just $20 shy of its all-time price low.

The TCL Designer Series Picture Frame TV is TCL's take on the Samsung Frame. It's a stylish TV than when turned off, can display artwork so that it blends into your living room. There are several sizes available, with prices starting from just $677.

Drumroll, please.......my favorite Black Friday TV deal this Wednesday (11/25) has got to be the TCL QM7L. Here's why: This TV won a Tom's Guide Editor's Choice Award and it also got the coveted Tom's Guide Award for Best Mini-LED TV of 2026.

It's TCL's first Super Quantum Dot (SQD) TV and it offers better contrast and color than rival Mini-LED TVs. All sizes are selling at an all-time price low right now. You can check out our TCL QM7L review for a full breakdown of the TV.

My colleague Dylan Haas reviews TVs for Tom's Guide. He's tested models like the Samsung S85H, Hisense U6 Pro, and more. He recently picked out the 11 Black Friday TV deals he recommends based on his testing. You can see his picks via the link above or check some of them out below.

The Hisense UR8 is an RGB Mini-LED 4K TV. That's a mouthful, but in a nutshell — RGB LED TVs use an array of ultra-small LEDs arranged in dimmable zones. However, unlike Mini-LEDs — RGB LEDs use red, green and blue LEDs. That results in brighter, purer colors than what we’ve come to expect from even the best TVs.

The UR8 is a Best Buy exclusive — along with many other RGB Mini-LEDs — and in typical Hisense fashion — it's disrupting the market with an insanely low price point. Case in point — this TV debuted at $1,699 and it's already down to $849, an all-time price low.

Ok, folks, here is my last blog update for today and it's a good one! The 48-inch LG B6 OLED TV is a Best Buy exclusive and right now it's selling for just $599. That's an insane price for such an amazing TV.

In our LG B6 OLED review we said it's an excellent TV for the price and it even beats the pricier LG C6 when it comes to SDR color accuracy. You also get some great gaming features, a cool design, and impressive black levels. It's our top pick for value and a sick deal for anyone looking to go OLED this year. Other sizes are also on sale, but sadly the 55-inch model appears out of stock at Amazon and Best Buy.

#3058. Yatsen (YSG) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Skincare now drives most sales as color cosmetics shrinks and margins hold steady.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:08PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Yatsen (YSG +1.20%) reported a total revenue decrease of 11.4% to RMB 884.5 million in the third quarter, as the company continued its strategic transition from color cosmetics to skincare. Management prioritized brand equity and long-term quality of growth over short-term scale, resulting in skincare brands accounting for 67.8% of total revenue. The company reported a net loss of RMB 129.0 million, influenced by a RMB 30.6 million impairment loss and a RMB 21.4 million noncash mark-to-market loss. For the fourth quarter, the company projected revenue growth between 0% and 10%, supported by performance during the Double 11 shopping festival.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Yatsen Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Irene Lyu, Vice President, Head of Strategic Investment and Capital Markets. Please go ahead.

Irene Lyu: Thank you, operator. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements relating to the company's future performance that are intended to qualify for the safe harbor from liability as established by the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act. Such statements are not guarantees of future performance and are subject to certain risks, uncertainties, assumptions and other factors. Some of these risks are beyond the company's control and could cause actual results to differ materially from those mentioned in today's press release and this discussion. A general discussion of the risk factors that could affect Yatsen's business and financial results is included in the company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The company does not undertake any obligation to update this forward-looking information, except as required by law. During today's call, management will also discuss certain non-GAAP financial measures for comparison purposes only. Please see the earnings release issued earlier today for a definition of non-GAAP financial measures and a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial results. Joining us today on the call from Yatsen's senior management are Mr. Jinfeng Huang, our Founder, Chairman and CEO; and Mr. Donghao Yang, our CFO and Director; and Mr. Li Wang, our Co-CFO. Management will also begin with prepared remarks, and the call will conclude with a Q&A session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

In addition, a webcast replay of this conference call will be available on Yatsen's Investor Relations website at ir.yatsenglobal.com. I will now turn the call over to Mr. Jinfeng Huang. Please go ahead, sir.

Jinfeng Huang: Thank you, Irene. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining our third quarter 2026 earnings call conference call. We continue to advance our strategic transformation in the third quarter. Total net revenues came in at RMB 884.5 million, down 11.4% year-over-year and slightly below our guidance. So, this was mainly driven by the streamlining of certain underperforming color cosmetics operations as part of our ongoing portfolio optimization. We are encouraged that our category mix is paying off. Skincare revenues grew 22.3% year-over-year and accounted for 67.8% of total net revenues, up from 49.2% a year ago, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth in skincare's revenue contribution.

Recently, we completed the divestiture of Pink Bear brand, further sharpening our focus on core skincare brands and reallocating resources towards our strategic priorities. This transaction is another step in simplifying our structure for sustainable growth. From a macro perspective, National Bureau of Statistics data indicates that China's beauty retail sales increased by 5.6% year-over-year in the third quarter of 2026, accelerating from the first half pace. The competitive environment remained intense, particularly in color cosmetics, where aggressive promotions and faster product cycles continue to pressure pricing for mass market brands. Against this backdrop, our focus remains on strengthening brand equity, deepening our consumer engagement and advancing our R&D-driven innovation.

Let me now walk you through the progress we made during this quarter. Focusing on strengthening brand equity and deepening consumer engagement, our portfolio delivered great progress this quarter. In September, CCTV.com interviewed DR.WU at CAME, coverage by official media that significantly expanded its exposure and reinforced its credibility with consumers. In the same month, we announced Liu Haoran as the brand's first ambassador, a pivotal step in broadening the brand's consumer reach and deepening its penetration across a wider demographic. On the product front, building on our signature Mandelic Acid franchise, both our core Mandelic Acid Essence and Brightening Renewal Toner obtained whitening certification from the National Medical Products Administration.

We subsequently launched upgraded versions carrying this whitening efficacy, expanding the franchise from its core acne and oil control benefits into everyday brightening. So, while DR.WU drove the portfolio's growth momentum, Galénic continued to anchor our premium skincare positioning. Building on its brightening heritage, Galénic strategically expanded into the anti-aging category. The launch of our eighth-generation Révélation Cream and the new Révélation Eye Cream represented a significant advance in our core offering. Alongside this, the introduction of the upgraded Galénic Extreme Youth Micro-Mask allowed us to capture strong consumer demand for intensive at-home spa treatment. For Eve Lom, several quarters of deliberate product portfolio expansion are now paying off.

Long known for its original balm cleanser, the brand now extended well beyond cleansing. The Renewal Treatment Eye Oil, introduced in late 2025 has become the proof point. In the third quarter, it alone contributed more than 10% of the brand's total GMV. On a combined basis, across our core online channels, including Tmall, Douyin and JD.com, Eve Lom ranked in the top 15 within the eye care category. Together, these results mark a meaningful step in Eve Lom's evolution from a single-product icon to a multi-category skincare brand. For Perfect Diary, we are glad to see that our overseas markets are showing positive momentum.

For the third quarter, overseas sales accounted for more than 20% of the brand's revenue and grew more than 20% year-over-year. For the group, that reduces Perfect Diary's dependence on a single highly promotional domestic market. We expect international markets to remain one of the brand's main growth engines as we widen distribution in markets where we already have a foothold. On R&D, our participation in this year's IFSCC Congress offered the most tangible external validation of our science agenda. This marks our fifth consecutive year at the Congress with 20 achievements accepted across 5 brands. What matters is not the count, but the breadth.

Our research spanned 11 of the 14 research areas the Congress was organized around and much of it is already tied to products on the market. Next, I would like to give you an update on Double 11, which concluded just 2 weeks ago. Our skincare brand performed strongly during this year's campaign. On Douyin official full period rankings, Galénic secured 10th place among international premium skincare brands and DR.WU ranked 15th across the beauty and personal care category. On Tmall's official full period rankings, DR.WU placed eighth among domestic skincare brands and Perfect Diary eighth among domestic color cosmetic brands, both within the top 10 on their respective domestic brand tables.

Galénic ranked 13th among premium skincare brands with its flagship store coming in 20th across all price tiers. Across these 2 platforms, we now have a meaningful presence in both the domestic and international premium segments, a testament of our multi-brand strategy and product-led growth. On sustainability, we also published our annual ESG report this quarter, reaffirming our commitment to long-term sustainable development. Looking ahead, our strategy remains consistent, a multi-brand portfolio powered by R&D, building towards a structurally healthier financial profile. We will continue to allocate resources with discipline, maintaining tight cost control while directing spending towards the brands with stronger equity and better potential.

With that, I will now turn the call over to our CFO, Donghao Yang, to walk through our financial details.

Donghao Yang: Thank you, David, and hello, everyone. Before I discuss the financial details, I would like to clarify that all financial numbers presented today are in renminbi and all percentage changes refer to year-over-year changes unless otherwise noted. Total net revenues for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 11.4% to RMB 884.5 million from RMB 998.4 million for the prior year period. The decrease was primarily driven by a 44.2% year-over-year decrease in net revenues from our color cosmetics brands, partially offset by a 22.3% year-over-year increase in net revenues from our skincare brands, which reflected the company's proactive brand portfolio optimization and deliberate SKU rationalization as part of our strategic transformation.

Gross profit for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 11.1% to RMB 693.6 million from RMB 780.5 million for the prior year period. Gross margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 78.4%, slightly up from 78.2% for the prior year period. Total operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 9.1% to RMB 785.1 million from RMB 864.1 million for the prior year period. As a percentage of total net revenues, total operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were 88.8% as compared with 86.5% for the prior year period. Fulfillment expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB 47.9 million as compared with RMB 61.8 million for the prior year period.

As a percentage of total net revenues, fulfillment expenses for the third quarter of 2026 decreased to 5.4% from 6.2% for the prior year period. The decrease was primarily attributable to further improvements in logistics efficiency. Selling and marketing expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB 642.9 million as compared with RMB 682.3 million for the prior year period. As a percentage of total net revenues, selling and marketing expenses for the third quarter of 2026 increased to 72.7% from 68.3% for the prior year period. The increase was primarily driven by strategic investments to broaden consumer awareness and build a long-term brand equity of our brand and effect of a lower revenue base.

General and administrative expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB 61.3 million as compared with RMB 80.2 million for the prior year period. As a percentage of total net revenues, general and administrative expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were 6.9% as compared with 8% for the prior year period. The decrease was primarily driven by a reduction in consulting fees as part of the company's cost control initiatives. Research and development expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB 33 million as compared with RMB 39.8 million for the prior year period.

As a percentage of total net revenues, research and development expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were 3.7% as compared with 4% for the prior year period. The decrease was primarily attributable to a slight reduction in product development expenses, while the company maintained a relatively stable level of R&D investment and continued to focus resources on key innovation projects. Loss from operations for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB 91.5 million as compared with RMB 83.6 million for the prior year period. Operating loss margin was 10.3% as compared with 8.4% for the prior year period.

Non-GAAP loss from operations for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB 71.9 million as compared with RMB 60.6 million for the prior year period. The non-GAAP operating loss margin was 8.1% as compared with 6.1% for the prior year period. Net loss for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB 129 million as compared with RMB 70.4 million for the prior year period. Net loss margin was 14.6% as compared with 7% for the prior year period.

The increase in net loss was primarily due to a RMB 30.6 million impairment loss from equity method investments, which primarily resulted from the partial transfer of the company's interest in the fund investment at cost and a RMB 21.4 million noncash mark-to-market loss on the convertible note issued in May 2026. Net loss attributable to Yatsen's ordinary shareholders per diluted ADS for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB 1.4 as compared with RMB 0.7 for the prior year period. Non-GAAP net loss for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB 67.7 million as compared with RMB 51.5 million for the prior year period. Non-GAAP net loss margin was 7.7% as compared with 5.2% for the prior year period.

Non-GAAP net loss attributable to Yatsen's ordinary shareholders per diluted ADS for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB 0.74 as compared with RMB 0.5 for the prior year period. As of September 30, 2026, the company had cash, restricted cash and short-term investments of RMB 816.3 million as compared with RMB 1.05 billion as of December 31, 2025. Net cash used in operating activities for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB 194.3 million as compared with RMB 126.8 million for the prior year period. The increase in cash outflow was primarily due to working capital movements ahead of the Double 11 shopping season, including inventory positioning and the timing of payables and receivables.

Looking at our business outlook for the fourth quarter of 2026, we expect our total net revenues to be between RMB 1.38 billion and RMB 1.52 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of approximately 0% to 10%. These forecasts reflect the company's current and preliminary views on the market and operational conditions, which are subject to change. With that, I would like to open the call to Q&A. Operator?

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The first question today comes from Maggie Huang with CICC.

Manqi (Maggie) Huang: This is Maggie Huang from CICC. I have two questions. My first question is that the management have mentioned the strong performance in Double 11 festival. So, is there any changes you have observed in the competitive landscape of the industry during this period? And my second question is that what steps will the company take to lift profitability? And how is the progress so far? That's my two questions.

Irene Lyu: Sure, Maggie. So, for your first question on Double 11. So, we have delivered a solid Double 11 performance, especially for skincare. Just to reiterate our performance for Double 11 for the ranking. For example, on Douyin's official full-period ranking, Galénic placed 10th among international premium skincare and DR.WU placed 15th in the whole beauty and personal skincare across all price tiers. And then on Tmall, DR.WU also placed eighth among domestic skincare brands and our Perfect Diary brand also placed eighth in domestic color cosmetics brands. And in addition, Galénic is among top 15 among premium skincare brands. So, quite good ranking for our Double 11 performance.

And in terms of the competitive landscape, what we have seen is for this year, the international brands are clearly more active, particularly in the premium skincare and also the clinical skincare. And also in that 2 categories, we have our brands also performed strongly, right, because Galénic is in premium skincare and also DR.WU in the more clinical and efficacy-driven skincare. So, that's for Double 11. And then for your second question, I think we can address your question from 3 angles, which are brand portfolio mix, channel mix and also product mix. So first, we're optimizing our brand portfolio mix.

Our skincare brand revenue contribution reached over 68% in the third quarter, so representing a 18% year-over-year increase compared with last year. And also recently, we completed the divestiture of the Pink Bear brand as part of our color cosmetics portfolio optimization. So, secondly, in terms of the channel mix, we aim to shift more from the lower-margin channels to higher-margin channels. And thirdly, for the product mix, we are increasing the contribution from the high gross margin products. So, we think in total, all these 3 initiatives will give us confidence in steadily expanding profitability while maintaining growth.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The next question comes from Jennifer Yuan with Haitong Securities.

Jennifer Yuan: This is Jennifer Yuan from Haitong Securities. So, congratulations on the strong growth of the skincare business. So, could the management team share more details on DR.WU's product portfolio development, particularly the sales momentum and consumer feedback for the PDRN series? Also, what are the plans for new product launches and hero product development going forward?

Irene Lyu: Sure. Let me give you progress on the product development. So -- as mentioned, right, the brand is doing well on the 2 core SKUs, the Mandelic Acid Serum and the Brightening Renewal Toner. And for this quarter, we already expanded these 2 core SKUs into new functional categories, which are whitening. So, both products get the whitening certification, and that will expand our product functional coverage and more consumer coverage. And then in terms of the PDRN, so we have seen the ingredients getting some buzz over a year or so, but we think it's still in a relatively early stage in terms of consumer acceptance.

So, right now, we are seeing our other new products are gaining more scale and also recognition at this stage, but we are still monitoring the development of the PDRN. And if the timing is right, then we will also continue to expand on that category.

Operator: This concludes our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Irene Lyu for any closing remarks.

Irene Lyu: Thank you, everyone, for once again joining us today. If you have any further questions, please feel free to contact us at Yatsen directly. Our IR contact information for both China and the U.S. can be found in today's press release. Thank you, and have a great day.

Operator: The conference has now concluded. Thank you for attending today's presentation. You may now disconnect.

#3055. Google Wallet comes to your iPhone – but without this feature

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > iOS

The new Google Wallet app brings Gemini agentic shopping to US-based iOS users - sorry, no tap-to-pay.

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits

The new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

#3054. Apple has iPads running macOS already, but don’t get too excited

With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A new report says that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either …

As iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but currently it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any plans to make it available outside the company.

Apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand new operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman says Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

The other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

However, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield issues may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

#3053. Not Jensen Huang. Not Data Centers. This Is the Real Reason Nvidia Could Soar in 2027.

Nvidia's next rally could have much less to do with accelerating earnings growth and more to do with how Wall Street actually values those profits.

By Adam Spatacco – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:15PM EST

The last several weeks have been unusually volatile for Nvidia (NVDA -3.94%) investors. Between the departure and subsequent reinstatement of founder Jensen Huang as CEO and growing concerns surrounding an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble, investors have had plenty to digest.

While much of the discussion around Nvidia focuses on its leadership and the unprecedented demand for data center infrastructure, another potential catalyst is hiding in plain sight. Interestingly, Nvidia stock could generate multibagger returns over the next year without the company exceeding Wall Street's growth expectations.

Let's explore why valuation expansion could be the biggest catalyst for Nvidia stock as 2027 approaches.

During the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended Oct. 25), Nvidia's revenue surged 103% year over year to $115.8 billion. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings per share (EPS) increased by 111%. Management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%.

Despite Nvidia's accelerating growth, shares are trading at a steep discount to their all-time high. Moreover, Wall Street analysts currently forecast Nvidia to generate $16.48 in EPS next fiscal year, implying a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 8.8 based on a current share price of $146.

Although Nvidia's earnings are overwhelmingly driven by its data center business, the company's valuation is influenced by several other factors. These include competition from Advanced Micro Devices and custom chip designs from Broadcom as well as macro factors like rising interest rates. These variables are impacting investor confidence in the sustainability of Nvidia's profits.

Nvidia's compressed valuation suggests investors are skeptical about the durability of the company's earnings power. However, several developments could change that perception throughout next year.

One of Nvidia's most underappreciated opportunities revolves around its software ecosystem. Between CUDA, Nvidia AI Enterprise, and its Nemotron family of open-weight models, the company is becoming increasingly embedded in how AI developers build and deploy applications.

Investors shouldn't necessarily focus on the amount of software revenue Nvidia generates today. Instead, it's important to understand how Nvidia is using software to make its chip empire more indispensable. As developers remain tied to both Nvidia hardware and software, the company is in a position to strengthen customer retention and increase switching costs. This should alleviate concerns that Nvidia's competitive advantage will erode as alternative chip architectures come to market.

Another catalyst is Nvidia's capital return strategy. In September, the company's board authorized an additional $150 billion in share repurchases, leaving approximately $227.3 billion available under its buyback program at the end of the third quarter. Even if net income remains constant, a reduction in outstanding shares can still increase EPS.

One of the most compelling aspects of Nvidia's current valuation profile is that the company doesn't necessarily need to exceed Wall Street's earnings expectations for the stock to appreciate. The table below illustrates how different valuation multiples would influence Nvidia's share price, assuming fiscal 2028 EPS remains constant at $16.48.

The big takeaway here is that Nvidia stock could more than double if investors are willing to assign the company a multiple of 20 times projected fiscal 2028 earnings. Even a relatively modest expansion to 15 times earnings would imply roughly 68% upside.

Investors may be overlooking how much pessimism is already reflected in Nvidia's stock price. Should the company simply meet existing expectations while demonstrating disciplined capital allocation and the durability of its competitive moat, Wall Street could gradually re-rate what Nvidia's earnings are worth.

Ultimately, Nvidia's next rally may have less to do with how much money the company makes and more to do with how much investors are willing to pay for those profits.

#3052. SpaceX Sued by 2 States Over Grok’s Sexualized Images of Women and Children

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

People used Grok to generate millions of "spicy mode" images.

Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s company violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

“When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones said. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable.”

Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

“It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”

Grok Imagine launched on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

“It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield said in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”

During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

In a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX said that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The company said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”

Earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

In July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The company seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

SpaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing users to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

Monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Big Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the company intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

#3051. 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

In today's job market, do applicants really have a choice of whether to comply with AI hiring tools?

Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report shows how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead

Samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

“For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”

Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a new Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber says that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”

After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”

Uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

#3047. The Flipper One is more than a Zero 2.0 – it’s a $399 Linux computer with a $13M Kickstarter

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

Backers are going big on the $759 Ultimate Bundle, but Flipper warns that rising RAM prices could affect production.

The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

The thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited

It could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be

The reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this new platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

The Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also says on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

#3046. Amazon Is Backing More Than 5 Gigawatts of New Nuclear by 2039. This Reactor Developer Could Cash In.

Amazon's 5-gigawatt nuclear push could give X-energy a powerful tailwind, but is the stock worth investing in right now?

By Courtney Carlsen – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:15PM EST

Hyperscalers face a big question: How do you feed power-hungry data centers while working toward net-zero carbon emissions? Amazon (AMZN -2.98%) is betting nuclear energy can help bridge that gap. The company is backing 5 gigawatts of new nuclear power by 2039, with small modular reactor developer X-energy (XE -5.16%) playing a key role.

With projects in the pipeline, Amazon's partnership gives X-energy a powerful backer and an opportunity to prove its nuclear technology can deliver. Could the artificial intelligence (AI) boom help turn this next-generation nuclear stock into a major growth opportunity?

In 2019, Amazon co-founded The Climate Pledge, which calls on signatories to reach net-zero carbon emissions by 2040. More recently, Amazon laid out plans to cut the carbon intensity of operations by 65% compared with 2019 levels.

A major component of Amazon's carbon-reduction goals involves nuclear energy, which provides carbon-free, reliable, 24/7 baseload power that data centers desperately need. Nuclear energy complements intermittent renewables, like wind and solar power, and numerous hyperscalers, including Microsoft, Meta Platforms, and Alphabet, are signing agreements for nuclear power.

Amazon launched its $2 billion Climate Pledge Fund in 2020, and it used some of those funds to become an early investor in X-energy in October 2024 during its Series C-1 financing round. Amazon provided much-needed project and development funds, and has been central in helping X-energy with the design, licensing, and build-out of its nuclear fuel facility.

X-energy develops the Xe-100 SMR, a high-temperature, gas-cooled nuclear reactor. The Xe-100 uses small graphite pebbles packed with uranium particles and coated in a high-temperature ceramic, and it uses helium gas for cooling. The reactor uses its core physics and heat-resistant fuel to naturally shut down the nuclear reaction and passively dissipate heat without pumps or human intervention.

SMRs are appealing because they are manufactured in modular factory units and can be linked together. For example, each Xe-100 produces 80 megawatts (MW) of electricity and can be linked together, like the 12-unit, 960 MW project planned in Indiana.

Amazon has been crucial for X-energy, helping it fund a four-unit project totaling 320 MW with Energy Northwest in central Washington. It has also committed funding to develop the 12-unit project with American Electric Power at the former coal plant in Indiana. Meanwhile, X-energy's project with Dow in Texas has cleared regulatory review for construction and hopes to deliver power by the early 2030s.

SMRs could completely change how we think about and deploy nuclear energy, and X-energy is one of many start-ups in the space. Amazon has helped X-energy clear regulatory hurdles and secure commercial agreements, giving it a massive leg up on competitors that lack similar backing.

X-energy could be a massive winner over the next decade as the nuclear renaissance unfolds. That said, X-energy's story is still being written, and it will be several years before it deploys its first reactors commercially, making the stock best suited for your watch list for now.

#3044. The Best Foldable Phones to Give This Holiday Season

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

For the tech enthusiast in your life, a foldable phone could be an interesting alternative to a traditional smartphone. We've rounded up our top picks, from book-style designs to flip phones.

If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.

After reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-new device? (You’ve been warned.)

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s said they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV shows on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

The iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

Multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

Perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.)

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

It’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

The phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

For most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

The Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

#3043. Your Google AI mode searches can stay private now with ‘temporary threads’ – here’s how

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With temporary threads, any searches you run in Google’s AI Mode won’t be associated with your account or saved to your chat history.

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training

New to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is currently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a new thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills

Certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:

Are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google says:

“Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google said on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”

Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes

ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

#3041. BYD vs. General Motors: Which Carmaker Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

BYD and GM are both leaning on very different engines, and the valuation gap between them may matter more than either company's EV pitch.

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 1:23PM EST

The global automotive market is shifting as electric vehicles challenge traditional engines. Investors must decide if high-growth BYD (BYDDF -2.14%) or the established legacy of General Motors (GM +1.99%) offers a better path forward.

BYD focuses on new-energy vehicles, batteries, and rail transit, establishing itself as a leader in the transition away from fossil fuels. General Motors relies on its massive scale and profit-heavy internal combustion engine sales to fund its own electric transformation. Both are competing for dominance in a rapidly changing transportation landscape.

BYD is a prominent player in the global automotive industry, which is a major part of consumer discretionary stocks. The company designs and sells new-energy vehicles while also operating in electronics, batteries, and rail transit systems. Its footprint covers more than 400 cities worldwide, supported by a massive workforce of nearly 869,622 employees.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $120.4 billion. The company reported a net income of approximately $4.7 billion during this time frame. Revenue growth was roughly negative 4.5% compared to the prior twelve-month period, reflecting recent shifts in the global market.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.7x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to show how a company funds its operations. Its current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, was approximately 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly negative $14.6 billion, representing the cash remaining after the business covers its day-to-day operations and capital equipment.

General Motors designs and builds a wide variety of trucks, crossovers, and cars, supported by more than 10,000 authorized dealerships globally. The company maintains strategic joint ventures for battery production and vehicle sales, particularly in the Chinese market. It also operates a captive finance arm to provide financing options for customers and dealers.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue was about $187 billion. Net income for the period was approximately $4.0 billion. This represented a revenue growth rate of nearly negative 0.3% as the company navigates the transition to new technology.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached roughly 2.1x. This metric indicates the relationship between total debt and shareholders' equity. The current ratio was close to 1.2x, representing the company's short-term liquidity. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached approximately $11.1 billion.

BYD faces significant challenges due to geopolitical trade tensions, as many regions are considering or imposing tariffs on imported vehicles. The company also operates in a crowded Chinese market where price wars can weigh on financial results. Furthermore, its global expansion requires significant capital investment in diverse regulatory environments.

General Motors appears to be the more conservatively priced option, as it carries a lower multiple of both earnings estimates and sales.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

General Motors has had a decent year, widening its market share in the U.S. to more than 17%, to stay the biggest car seller in the country. Also, hybrids like the Chevy Equinox and Blazer and the EV Cadillac Lyriq have been better sellers than expected, calming some fears that GM was falling behind in the trend toward hybrids and EVs.

The company has also been aggressively buying back shares, which supports the share price in the market and makes profitability appear to be improving on the per-share level. GM also shifted its shares to the Nasdaq Stock Market recently to try and get itself listed on the Nasdaq 100 index, which would also be supportive for shares, given that about $1.4 trillion in assets are indexed to the Nasdaq 100. The company is also lauded on Wall Street for handling the various Trump tariff issues that had generated fears the business would be adversely impacted.

That said, top-line growth is slow, with 2027 revenue seen rising $3 billion to $189 billion and net income exceeding $12 billion, up from about $9 billion expected for full year 2026.

Turning to BYD, while the company doesn't have a U.S. presence, it is one of the top automakers in China. The automaker's September vehicle sales increased about 17% compared to the same month in 2025, headlined by a remarkable 154% jump in overseas shipments of passenger vehicles and pickups. It's part of the company's goal of catching Toyota Motor Co. (TM +2.62%) as the world's largest automaker. Overseas sales were about 39% of BYD's sales in the third quarter. Yet it has its domestic challenges, with Q3 China sales declining more than 18% for BYD, due to intense pricing competition and a hurting Chinese consumer.

Still, foreign sales should help BYD push 2027 sales up 16% in its reporting currency of Chinese yuan, to about $145 billion at today's exchange rate.

So which stock to go with? BYD's push into Europe appears to be going very well, but that is counterbalanced by domestic problems. GM is a bargain price at a forward P/E ratio of 5.8x. The Great Recession bailout by the U.S. federal government showed how important GM is to the U.S. economy. The bet here is that GM's leading position in the world's second-largest car market, the U.S., will continue to hold, and management will continue to find ways to improve returns to shareholders.

#3040. Uber, Nuro and Lucid Begin Fully Driverless Testing With Their Luxury Robotaxi

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The Lucid Gravity robotaxi is one step closer to a commercial launch.

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies said Tuesday.

The partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

Now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said. They plan to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber plans to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

“Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an important milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, said in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”

Nuro says it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

In May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the company the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

Uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

The Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

It’s been a big year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.
